2011_019_050311regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of May 3, 2011, held at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. It carries recognitions (Outstanding Support Staff Award to Smith Middle School head custodian David Jones, a list of 2010-2011 retirees, and National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 2-6, 2011), the April 19, 2011 minutes, four bid items, and a report on the Oakland Schools proposed fiscal year 2011-12 budget, which shows total revenue of $271.4 million against a total expenditure budget of $283.7 million.
2011_019_050311regmtg.page:
**What this is**
Board agenda and supporting packet for the Troy School District (Troy, Michigan) Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, May 3, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

**Recognition**
- David Jones, Head Custodian at Smith Middle School, receives the 2010-2011 Outstanding Support Staff Award; he started as a custodian in November of 1995 and was chosen by a committee of TESA, TESPA and non-represented personnel.
- Retirees are introduced, among them Sally Dorset, Media Specialist at Hamilton Elementary (42 years), Ron O'Hara, Principal of Troy Union Elementary (40 years), and Dan Stevens, Music Teacher at Athens High (38 years). Board President Nancy Philippart presents each retiree a clock.
- Resolution supporting National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 2-6, 2011.

**April 19, 2011 minutes (consent item)**
Called to order 7:03 p.m.; approximately 215 members of the audience. Resolution 11-034 recites a projected 2011-2012 operating deficit estimated between $13.6 million and $16 million and authorizes administration to implement approximately $6 million in budget adjustments and draw approximately $7.6 million of existing fund equity. Resolution 11-037 awarded copy paper to Contract Paper Group, Inc. (formerly RIS Paper) for $63,579.60 after 11-036 rescinded the earlier award of Bid 9702 to D & P Management. Resolution 11-033 accepted the resignations of Scott Bryan, Director of Technology (effective May 6, 2011) and Judy Hunsberger, Principal of Morse Elementary (effective June 30, 2011); 11-038 opposed transferring School Aid Fund dollars to higher education. Adjourned 10:16 p.m.

**Bid awards before the Board**

| Item | Bid no. | Vendor | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Athletic supplies | 9703 | Anaconda Sports / Dimmer Warren Enterprises / ForSports / Cannon Sports | $2,502.59 / $6,798.20 / $6,113.41 / $568.32 | 2011/12 General |
| Football supplies | 9709 | Tri-County Sports | $13,328.00 | 2011/12 General |
| Computers, Troy Career Center | 9707 | Inacomp TSG | $29,117.00 | 2010/11 General |
| Masonry, Baker Middle School | 9704 | M. J. Chisholm | $6,800.00 | 2004 Capital Projects |
| Lockers, Baker Middle School | 9705 | Steel Equipment Company | $16,300.00 | 2004 Capital Projects |

Bids 9703 and 9709 together total $29,310.52; the two Baker Middle School awards total $23,100.00.

**Technology Support Services (Bid 9708)**
Bids opened April 19, 2011 on an RFP dated April 5, 2011; six responses from Specialized Electronics LLC, SRC Pro-Video Service, Edwards and Company, Netarx, Integrated Support Strategies, Inc. and Inacomp TSG. The three low bidders are companies owned and operated by current District staff. The resolution authorizes contract negotiations with SRC Pro-Video Service, Edwards and Company, and Specialized Electronics, LLC. Director of Technology Scott Bryan's worksheet assumes 24.59% FICA plus retirement, $17,530 estimated full family insurance and 2080 hours per year, and shows estimated Year 1 savings to the District of $65,222.81.

**Curriculum report**
iPad Challenge pilot begun in Fall 2010; the District purchased 44 devices. Presented by Ron Keoleian, Michelle Slaviero (Boulan Park) with her students, and Scott Bryan.

**Oakland Schools proposed FY 2011-12 budget (report by Mark Rajter)**
Required by Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624): the ISD submits its budget by May 1 and constituent boards adopt a resolution of support or disapproval by June 1.

| Measure | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Total revenue | $271.4 million |
| Total expenditure budget | $283.7 million |
| General Education Fund revenue / expenditures | $17.8M / $18.0M |
| Special Education Fund revenue and expenditures | $132.8 million |
| Career Focused Education Fund revenue / expenditures | $32.7M / $32.5M |
| Grants and funded projects | $74.5M |
| Total Oakland Schools bonded debt | $60,885,000 |

Property tax collection declines 22.7% from FY 2008 to FY 2014, an accumulative loss of $186.5 million against an FY 2008 base year levy of $216.9 million.
2011_019_050311regmtg.verbose:
**Meeting and agenda**
Board agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of May 3, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; the district address 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000, appears on the notice. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August.

**Recognition**
David Jones, Head Custodian at Smith Middle School, is named the 2010-2011 Outstanding Support Staff Award winner; the resolution, signed the third day of May, 2011, notes he started as a custodian in November of 1995 and was chosen by a committee of the Troy Educational Secretaries Association (TESA), the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (TESPA) and non-represented personnel.
Retirees introduced for the end of the 2010-2011 school year, with service length: Paul Boman (Skilled Trades, Buildings and Grounds, 25); Camille Conley (ESL, Niles Community Education, 16); Sheri DeCew (Media Specialist, Wattles and Morse, 30); Sally Dorset (Media Specialist, Hamilton, 42); W. Charles Foster (Special Education Teacher Consultant, Athens, 24); Deanna Francis (2nd Grade, Schroeder, 22); Charles Garofali (Science, Larson, 34); Wylie Gerdes (Network Administrator, Services Building, 13); John Getzan (Social Worker, Martell, 28); Linda Hannon (Director of Special Education, Services Building, 32); Patricia Kleefuss (Media Specialist, Baker, 13); Diane Kohut (Child Care Assistant, Hamilton, 20); Barbara Kowalski (Computer Technician, Niles Community Center, 15); Cynthia Laskowsky (2nd Grade, Troy Union, 15); Sue Last (Resource Room, Wattles, 28); Sharon Moore (Adult Education, Niles Community Center, 17); Suzanne O'Hara (Interim Principal, Morse, 16); Ron O'Hara (Principal, Troy Union, 40); Janet Peplin (PACE, Troy Union, 32); Nancy Rademacher (English, Athens, 25 1/2); Joan Riley (3rd Grade, Schroeder, 26); Harry Sahourieh (Skilled Trades, 23); Melissa Solley (Media Specialist, Athens, 30); Nancy Stachowiak (Payroll Secretary, Administration Building, 32); Dan Stevens (Music, Athens, 38); Tim Storch (History, Athens, 28); Pam Teimorzadeh (Science, Athens, 12); Darla Van Hoey (French, Athens, 36); John Walker (Political Science, Athens, 35); Janet Weil (English, Troy High, 25). For approximately twenty (20) minutes before the meeting the monitors display a visual recognition of retirees; Jasen Witt reads each name and Board President Nancy Philippart presents a clock. A third resolution supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 2-6, 2011.

**April 19, 2011 minutes**
President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with members Edmunds, Hauff, Fleming, Malven, Miletti and Underwood present, plus Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Bryan, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter and Witt; and approximately 215 members of the audience. Ewa Ostrowski (Smith) was middle school Teacher of the Year, Trevor Smith (Troy High) high school, and Caryn Leonard (Barnard) elementary and overall District Teacher of the Year; Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union awarded mini-grants to teachers at Athens, Barnard, Bemis, Hamilton, Larson, Smith and Wattles. Actions, all 7 ayes and 0 nays: Item 5.D., Non-Renewal Teacher Contract, deleted from the consent agenda; 11-032 approving the March 1 and March 15, 2011 Workshop minutes and the Treasurer's Report for February and March 2011; 11-033 accepting resignations from Scott Bryan, Director of Technology, effective May 6, 2011, and Judy Hunsberger, Principal, Morse Elementary School, effective June 30, 2011; 11-034 reciting a projected 2011-2012 operating deficit estimated between $13.6 million and $16 million and authorizing approximately $6 million in budget adjustments plus a draw on existing fund equity of approximately $7.6 million under a three-year plan; 11-035 approving reductions in certified staff; 11-036 rescinding the Bid 9702 copy paper award to D & P Management; 11-037 awarding copy paper to Contract Paper Group, Inc. (formerly known as RIS Paper) for $63,579.60 from the 2010/2011 General Fund; 11-038 opposing diversion of School Aid Fund dollars to community colleges and higher education, citing Proposal A of 1994; and 11-039 scheduling a Special Board Meeting for Tuesday, May 17, 2011. Speakers included Janet McGrail (TESPA president), Janine Craft, Bruce Bloomingdale, Ann Marie Wattai, Doreen Higgins and Terry Navratil, on teacher aide reductions, school funding, the GROW program transition coordinator and outsourcing school secretaries; Karl Schmidt of Consumer Insights, Inc. presented the Troy Teachers Technology Training Study (T4). Under 11-031 the Board entered closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by roll call 7-0 at 9:07 p.m., reconvened at 9:18 p.m. and adjourned at 10:16 p.m.; minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**Fall athletic supplies (Bids 9703 and 9709)**
April 25, 2011 memorandum from Frank E. Lams, Purchasing Consultant, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, to Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services. Bids opened February 28, 2011; because no qualified responses came in for several football items for Athens and Troy High Schools, a second bid was opened April 19. The first bid went to 15 potential bidders with 12 responses (one "No Bid"), the second to 13 potential bidders with nine responses (four "No Bid"); Athletic Director M. Jolly recommended the awards. Bid 9703: Anaconda Sports $2,502.59, Dimmer Warren Enterprises $6,798.20, ForSports $6,113.41, Cannon Sports $568.32, subtotal $15,982.52. Bid 9709: Tri-County Sports $13,328.00. Combined total $29,310.52 against the 2011/12 General Fund. The 9709 tabulation for football pants and shoulder pads lists column totals of $4,633.88, $12,047.55, $13,328.00, $13,906.60 and $17,286.00 across Dimmer Warren, ForSports, Tri-Custom Sports, BSN Sports and Riddell/All American; the 16-page 9703 tabulation covers Athens and Troy High football, soccer, volleyball, swim, golf and cross country plus Boulan and Larson girls basketball.

**iPad demonstration**
In the Fall of 2010 the District piloted Apple iPads as part of the next year's laptop replacement project, purchasing 44 devices for the iPad Challenge. Presenters: Ron Keoleian, District Technology Coordinator; Michelle Slaviero, Boulan Park Social Studies teacher, with her students; and Scott Bryan, Director of Technology. Winning entries: Baker Middle School, "The Amazing Race: Latin America" by Kathryn Loch and Janet Herberholz (6th grade Social Studies); Troy Union Elementary, "Fact Power (Math Power for Life)" by Denice Pysh (5th grade math); Boulan Park Middle School, City Government Budget Simulation by Michelle Slaviero (8th grade US History/Government); Larson Middle School, "Math in the Real World & Common Assessment Review" by Shelley McHugh (6th/7th grade Pre-Algebra); and Smith Middle School, "iPad: Enhancing and Extending Online Learning" by Mary MacNair (8th grade Earth Science).

**Computers, Troy Career Center (Bid 9707)**
Bids for a lab and server at the Troy Career Center were released March 17, 2011 and opened March 31, 2011, sent to 16 potential bidders with nine responding (one "No Bid"). The resolution awards the bid to Inacomp TSG for $29,117.00 from the 2010/11 General Fund. Frank Lams' memorandum is dated April 12, 2011; Scott Bryan's April 13, 2011 memorandum (Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois, 248-823-5090) states there were eight bid responses, that he analyzed the two apparent lowest solutions, Inacomp TSG and Aprisa Technology, and that Inacomp complies with specifications and includes a mandatory alternate upgrading desktops from a dual core to a quad core processor at no extra cost. The tabulation covers 1 server and 28 desktops; column totals under Aprisa Technology, EnPointe Technologies Sales and Sehi Computer Products are $29,656.64, $45,478.43 and $20,300.00, with further columns of $37,060.74, $25,420.92, $29,117.00, $35,331.97 and $36,880.74. Line pricing recorded includes an HP ML330 G6 server at $6,241.00 with 28 HP 6000 Pro SFF desktops at $817.00 for $22,876.00, a $4,488.00 server with $898.88 desktops, Dell Optiplex 780 at $1,133.33 and Grace J-Box N425 at $907.89. CDW-G returned No Bid; HP, MA Labs, Multiwave Educational, Netech, New Tech Solutions, Red Level Networks and Suntel did not respond.

**Lockers and masonry, Baker Middle School (Bids 9704 and 9705)**
Bids were opened April 13, 2011 under two separate requests for proposals. The masonry bid went to 16 potential bidders with four responding, one disqualified for lack of the required Familial Disclosure form (Royal Restoration); the locker bid went to 16 potential bidders with five responding, one "No Bid" (D.R. Storage Systems). Ken Miller, Director of Operations, recommended the awards in Frank Lams' April 25, 2011 memorandum. Masonry is awarded to M. J. Chisholm for $6,800 and lockers to Steel Equipment Company for $16,300, together $23,100.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. Bid 9705 covers Phase I and Phase II locker rooms and Phase III corridor lockers with line items for relocating lockers and installing 40 and 60 frames; bidder totals recorded are $16,300.00, $16,400.00, $20,769.00 and $22,873.45 among Steel Equipment, Rayhaven Group, R.E. Leggette and Schiffler Equipment. Bid 9704 covers concrete block installation, base installation and repair/replace ceiling grid, with M.J. Chisholm's line items of $5,793.00, $582.00 and $425.00 totaling $6,800.00 alongside competing totals of $21,090.00 and $17,525.00 from Luigi Ferdinandi & Son Cement and Mark 1 Restoration.

**Technology Support Services (Bid 9708)**
Bids for third-party contracting of technology support services were opened April 19, 2011 on an RFP dated April 5, 2011, with six responses: Specialized Electronics, LLC, SRC Pro-Video Service, Edwards and Company, Netarx, Integrated Support Strategies, Inc. and Inacomp TSG. The resolution authorizes administration to enter contract negotiations with SRC Pro-Video Service, Edwards and Company, and Specialized Electronics, LLC. Scott Bryan's April 25, 2011 memorandum states the three apparent low bidders are all companies owned and operated by current District staff: SRC Pro-Video Service (AV Specialist), in operation more than 20 years; Specialized Electronics LLC (Telecom and Help Desk Specialists), operating since 1998; and Edwards and Company (Computer Systems Specialist), to be formed if selected. In every instance except one Help Desk response, bids from traditional organizations equal or exceed District compensation; the only bidder concern was the 30 day window for retirees returning to work. The comparison worksheet assumes 24.59% FICA plus retirement, $17,530 estimated full family insurance and 2080 hours per year, listing per employee TSD hourly, TSD annual, hourly equivalent with benefits, TSD annual including benefits, bid hourly Year 1, bid annual and savings: Chris McFatridge, Telecom Specialist, $25.69, $53,435.20, $40.44, $84,104.92, $34.00, $70,720.00, $13,384.92; Jill Weaver, Help Desk Specialist, $18.52, $38,521.60, $31.50, $65,524.06, $25.00, $52,000.00, $13,524.06; Bill Edwards, Computer Systems Specialist, $25.69, $53,435.20, $40.44, $84,104.92, $30.45, $63,336.00, $20,768.92; Stan Coldicott, Audio/Visual Systems Specialist, $25.69, $53,435.20, $40.44, $84,104.92, $32.00, $66,560.00, $17,544.92; estimated Year 1 savings to the District $65,222.81. Three-year contract pricing: Specialized Electronics Help Desk $25.00 / $26.00 / $27.00 and Telecommunications $34.00 / $35.00 / $36.00 base, with emergency/holiday/weekend rates of $37.50 / $39.00 / $40.50 and $51.00 / $52.50 / $54.00; SRC Pro-Video $32.00 base and $39.00 emergency each year; Edwards & Company $30.45 / $30.95 / $31.45 base and $45.68 / $46.43 / $47.18 emergency. Netarx, Inacomp TSG and Integrated Support Strategies quoted higher, including Netarx Year 1 base rates of $50.78, $49.48, $27.08 and $45.31. A forwarded April 19, 2011 email from Bryan to Rajter reviews 20 RFP evaluation criteria, including five years of experience supporting an organization with a minimum of 1,000 employees.

**Oakland Intermediate School District proposed budget (report by Mark Rajter)**
Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624), effective in 2004, requires each ISD to submit its proposed budget to constituent districts by May 1 and each constituent board to adopt a resolution of support or disapproval by June 1. Property tax decline from base year FY 2008: -.0075% in FY 2008-09; -3.8% / $8.2M in FY 2009-10; -11.75% / $32.9M in FY 2010-11; -7.5% / $46.7M in FY 2011-12; -1.5% / $49.3M in FY 2012-13; -0.0% / $49.3M in FY 2013-14. Annual collection declines 22.7% from FY 2008 to FY 2014, accumulative loss $186.5 million, FY 2008 base year levy $216.9 million, FY 2014 expected levy $167.6 million. Revenue assumptions include a 7.5% property tax revenue decrease, a 1.5% investment return, General Education Section 81 reduced by 5%, and Special Education Section 51a.8 eliminated at $2.8 million, with all other State Aid held flat. Total revenue is $271.4 million and the total expenditure budget $283.7 million, comprising transfers to LEAs $128.2, grant related expenditures $74.5, salaries and benefits $46.6, purchase services $12.2, supplies, materials, dues and fees 10.7, capital outlay and other $9.5, utilities $1.1 and transfers to other funds $1.0 (dollars in millions). The General Education Fund shows revenue of $17.8 million (property tax $10.1M, 56% of total; other local $3.7M; state sources $3.5M; other financing sources $.5M) and expenditures of $18.0 million (general administration $1.5M, finance and operations $6.5M, instructional services $9.2M, plant and fixed charges and LEA transfers $.8M). Five-year forecast, 2011-12 through 2015-16: revenue 17,892,900 / 18,038,850 / 18,231,077 / 18,429,443 / 18,582,956; expenditures 18,031,900 / 18,266,991 / 18,486,737 / 18,743,464 / 19,034,345; operating deficit (139,000) / (228,141) / (255,661) / (314,021) / (451,390); unassigned balance 2,172,000 / 1,943,859 / 1,688,199 / 1,374,178 / 859,749 plus 29,000 assigned for prepaid, inventory and deposits; total 2,201,000 / 1,972,859 / 1,717,199 / 1,403,178 / 951,788; unreserved fund balance at 12.12% / 10.80% / 9.29% / 7.49% / 5.00% of expenditures. The Special Education Fund shows revenue and expenditures of $132.8 million (property tax $128.6M, 96% of revenue; other local $1.4M; state sources $2.6M; program supervision and direction $2.4M; program operations $7.2M; plant and fixed charges $6.8M; LEA transfers and program subsidies $116.4M). FY 2012 special education program support and subsidies total $116,410,600: PA-18 Base Distribution $114,080,600, Group Homes $1,200,000, SEI Regional Day Treatment $450,000, Extraordinary Contingency $250,000, Michigan Rehab Services Cash Match $180,000, Havenwick $150,000 and Section 24 subsidy $100,000; the PA-18 Base Distribution declined $(29.2M) from FY 2010. Five-year forecast: revenue 132,849,200 / 131,646,025 / 131,995,730 / 132,346,477 / 132,377,299; expenditures 132,789,100 / 131,520,830 / 131,882,006 / 132,234,477 / 132,264,739; operating excess 60,100 / 82,746 / 125,195 / 113,724 / 112,580; restricted center program facility renovation 386,000 / 486,000 / 586,000 / 686,000 / 786,000; restricted special education 835,700 / 860,895 / 874,619 / 887,093 / 899,653; total 1,221,700 / 1,346,895 / 1,460,619 / 1,573,093 / 1,685,653; fund balance net of LEA operating transfers 5.00% each year. The Career Focused Education Fund shows revenue of $32.7 million (property tax $31.5 M, 96%; other local $0.6 M; state sources $.4 M; other financing sources $0.2 M) and expenditures of $32.5 million (campus and other program administration $21.3 M, plant and fixed charges $6.0 M, LEA transfers and direct program operations $4.9 M, facility and technology maintenance and renovations $0.3 M), Forecast revenue 32,793,500 / 32,485,508 / 32,573,281 / 32,673,274 / 32,673,585; expenditures 32,510,000 / 33,803,771 / 32,852,911 / 33,392,651 / 34,011,770; operating excess 292,500 then deficits (1,318,263) / (279,630) / (719,376) / (1,338,185); restricted balance 5,356,100 / 4,037,837 / 3,758,208 / 3,039,831 / 1,700,646, at 16.48% / 11.94% / 11.44% / 9.10% / 5.00% of expenditures. Grants and funded projects total $74.5M, comprising new awards of $51.8M and carry over of $22.7M, with $62.8M transferred directly to districts and $11.7M administered by the ISD (including JobLink at $5.5M). FY 2012 district debt lists GEF principal of $4,415,000 with an average annual payment of $750,000, CFEF principal of $41,670,000 at $3,100,000, QSCB principal of $14,800,000 at $850,000, and total Oakland Schools bonded debt of $60,885,000 at $4,700,000; debt service for the 2003 Administration Building project bond and the QSCB issue is pre-funded in Debt Service Funds 310 and 313, and the 2007 campus renovations bond is pre-funded in Debt Service Fund 312 through FY 2019.

**Closed session**
The packet closes with a resolution to go into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a), to discuss negotiations and the superintendent's evaluation, with a roll call listing Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti, Philippart, Underwood and Edmunds.
